transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm only here because... look, my husband is the one who made the appointment. Him and, well, pretty much everyone at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. Like I'm just making things up. But I'm not. I know exactly what's going on down on the floor. I move freight, right? I load the trucks, and I know how to count my own pallets. 

But lately—and this has been going on for a little while now—they’ve been watching every single move I make. I can see them out of the corner of my eye when I'm working the floor. And it's not just staring, they are actually going in behind my back and changing my pallet counts. I'll stack and wrap fifty, and suddenly the log says I only did thirty. They’re doing it on purpose, and my husband just sighs and tells me I need to see a doctor, but he doesn't even work there! He doesn't see how they stand by the loading dock and track what I'm doing. 

It's because that supervisor spot opened up. I know it is. They are doing everything they can to mess with my numbers and sabotage me so I don't get that promotion. And now everyone is treating me like I'm the one losing my mind just because I finally caught on to their little game.
You mentioned this has been going on for a little while—can you tell me exactly how many weeks or months you've noticed people watching you and changing your pallet counts?

Well, if you want exact... I mean, I can give you exact because I've actually been having to keep track of it all. It’s been about eight months now. Yeah, eight months. I remember because it was right after we did the big quarterly inventory sweep, and that’s when I first started hearing the voices. 

At first, I thought, you know, maybe it's just the echo in the warehouse—it’s this huge corrugated metal building, sounds bounce around off the racking all the time. But no, I'd be all the way in the back by the oversized freight, totally alone, sweeping up shrink wrap, and I'd hear them. The voices just whispering about my numbers, telling me they were coming for my spot, telling me to watch my back. And that feeling, that awful prickle on the back of your neck when you just know someone is burning a hole into you with their eyes? That started right at the exact same time. 

Eight whole months of this. Every single day I clock in, I feel them watching me from the catwalks, and I hear the whispering, and then I go to check the computer log and my pallets are short. My husband acts like I just woke up yesterday and started making this all up out of thin air, but I have been dealing with this for eight months straight. You try stacking heavy freight for eight months while people are actively trying to ruin your life and the voices won't let up about it. It’s not just a 'little while,' it's been most of the year, and I'm just so tired of having to defend myself when I'm the one doing the actual work out there.
During these past eight months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or extremely elevated and energetic, separate from the concerns about being watched?

Well, I mean... it's not like I'm depressed or crying all day, if that's what you mean by low. Honestly, it's almost the opposite sometimes. There are these stretches—like, days at a time—where I just feel so... fired up. Like I have this electricity running through my arms and legs, and nobody can slow me down. I get to the warehouse and I'm just throwing boxes, wrapping pallets in record time, just flying through the aisles. I feel like I could work a double shift, go home, clean the whole house, and not even need to sleep. It’s this intense energy, like my engine is just revving and revving. 

But the thing is, when I get like that, I have zero patience for anyone getting in my way. Especially my husband. I mean, I'll be in this zone, getting things done, and he’ll come at me with some tiny, stupid question about what the kids are having for dinner or if I remembered to pay the water bill or what my shift schedule is for next week. And I just... I snap. I go from zero to a hundred and just bite his head off. It feels like he’s doing it on purpose to drag me down, you know? Like he’s trying to control me or micromanage me when I'm clearly operating on a higher level than him. 

He tells me I'm being mean or that I'm overreacting, but he just doesn't get it. When I have that kind of momentum, when I'm finally feeling good and powerful and like I can take on the whole world—and those guys at the warehouse—I don't have time for his little interrogations. It just makes me so incredibly irritated, like this hot flash of anger right in my chest, because why can't he just let me be great? Why does he have to try and put a leash on me? So yeah, I guess my mood gets elevated, but it just makes me realize how much everyone else is dragging their feet.

During the times when you're NOT feeling that surge of energy or irritability—when your mood is more your usual self—do you still hear the whispering voices and still feel that people are watching and changing your counts?

Well, yeah, of course I do. I mean, it's not like the guys at the warehouse just take a break from trying to ruin my life just because I'm having a regular week. Like, there was this stretch—maybe a month or two ago, I think it was right around the time my youngest had that terrible ear infection, so I was really focused on that—and I actually had a few quieter weeks. I wasn't feeling all revved up like a motor, you know? I was actually sleeping closer to normal, maybe getting six or seven hours a night instead of just two or three, and I wasn't racing around the house trying to scrub the baseboards at midnight or snapping at my husband every time he opened his mouth. I was just... normal. Just going to work, doing my shift, coming home, making dinner. 

But even then, even when I was totally calm and just going through the motions of a regular week, the voices didn't stop. I'd be walking down aisle four, just minding my own business, not feeling angry or energetic at all, and I'd still hear that whisper. Clear as day. Just right by my ear, telling me to check the logs, telling me they were messing with my numbers again. And they were! I'd go look, and the pallet counts would be wrong. So, yeah, it doesn't matter if I'm feeling like I can take on the world or if I'm just having a regular, boring Tuesday where I'm tired and just want to go home. The whispering is always there, and the sabotage is always happening. It never really stops, no matter how much sleep I get or how calm I'm feeling. They just keep at it, relentless, like they have nothing better to do than try to push me out.

Looking back over the full eight months, would you say these intense energetic, irritable stretches have taken up most of that time, or have the calmer, more normal weeks like the one during your son's ear infection actually made up the bigger portion?

Well, if I really look back at the calendar and add it all up... it’s definitely the fired-up times. Without a doubt. I mean, if you're asking what took up the biggest chunk of the time, those quiet weeks are really just the exception, not the rule. For more than half of this whole eight-month stretch, honestly, I have had those fired-up periods where I sleep very, very little and just take on way too much. 

Or at least, my husband says it's too much. I'll be running on maybe two or three hours of sleep for weeks on end, volunteering to stay late at the warehouse to break down the extra incoming freight because nobody else moves fast enough, and then I come home and decide the entire garage needs to be swept out and reorganized right that exact second. And because I'm doing all of that, and my brain is just moving a million miles a minute, I get so unbelievably irritable when anyone tries to slow me down. 

It’s been the vast majority of the year like this. Out of the eight months, I'd say easily five or six of them have been me just running on pure electricity. Just non-stop energy, barely ever closing my eyes, taking on every single project at work and at home, and just snapping at people who don't get it. It feels like I'm a freight train with no brakes, and everyone around me is just standing on the tracks waving their arms, trying to tell me to stop and go to bed. The calm periods, like that time with my son's ear infection, they happen, sure, but they go by so fast. And then boom, I'm right back to being totally wired and getting furious at my husband for just asking a simple question and interrupting my flow. So yeah, definitely way more than half the time has been me just running completely hot like that.

Critically, these psychotic symptoms persisted during a distinct multi-week period when mood was euthymic (normal sleep, no irritability/grandiosity, calm behavior during son's illness), confirming psychosis independent of mood episodes—ruling out Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (F30.2). Because mood episodes were present for the majority of the total illness duration while psychotic symptoms also occurred in the absence of mood symptoms for a significant period (weeks), this pattern is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Schizophrenia (F20.0), which would require mood episodes to be brief/minor relative to psychotic illness duration.
